[size=3][/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=endorsements][size=3]https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=endorsements[/size][/url][/quote]



[size=5][b]What This Mod Does[/b][/size]

This mod eliminates lag caused by the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1063]Automate[/url] mod by implementing intelligent idle detection. In vanilla Automate, the mod continuously scans and processes ALL machine groups across your ENTIRE farm every single tick (60 times per second), regardless of where you are or what you're doing. When you have extensive automation setups with hundreds of machines spread across multiple locations, this constant background processing causes significant performance degradation - lag spikes, stuttering, and reduced FPS, especially when you're actively exploring other maps.

Automate No More Lag stops this wasteful background processing entirely when you're moving around. The automation system only runs when you're standing still (idle), completely eliminating CPU overhead during active gameplay.

[center]﻿[youtube]af32OHlptUM[/youtube][/center]


[line]

[size=5][b]How It Works[/b][/size]

The mod uses Harmony to patch Automate's MachineManager at the highest level, intercepting automation before it even begins iterating through machine groups.

[size=4][b]Traditional Automate Behavior:[/b][/size]
[code]
Every game tick (60 times per second):
- Automate scans ALL machine groups it constantly scans even nothing to process
- Checks inputs/outputs for EVERY machine
- Processes item transfers across entire farm
- This happens even when you're in Pelican Town, the mines, etc.
= Constant CPU usage regardless of player activity
[/code]

[size=4][b]With Automate No More Lag:[/b][/size]
[code]
Every game tick:
- Mod checks: Is player moving?
- YES: Automate is completely stopped (returns false before any processing)
- NO: Has player been idle for threshold duration?
- YES: Automate runs normally
- NO: Automate remains stopped
= ZERO CPU overhead when moving, normal automation when idle
[/code]

[line]

[size=5][b]Patch Strategy[/b][/size]

[b]Primary Method (Zero Overhead):[/b]
The mod patches [font=Courier New]MachineManager.AutomateAll()[/font] or equivalent automation entry points. When the player is moving, the patch returns [font=Courier New]false[/font] immediately, preventing Automate from executing ANY of its machine scanning logic.

[b]Fallback Method (Minimal Overhead):[/b]
If the primary patch fails to find the manager method, the mod falls back to patching individual [font=Courier New]MachineGroup.Automate()[/font] methods. While less efficient, this still prevents machine processing for each group.

[line]

[size=5][b]Configuration Options[/b][/size]

[i]Configure via [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url][/i]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/41945/41945-1770182546-37951973.png[/img]﻿﻿﻿[/center]


[line]

[size=5][b]Idle Detection System[/b][/size]

The mod tracks player position every game tick (60 times per second) and implements a timer-based idle detection algorithm:

[b]Always Processing (Automation Runs):[/b]
[list]
[*]Player has been stationary for configured duration (default 8 seconds)
[*]Idle detection feature is disabled
[/list]

[b]Never Processing (Automation Stopped):[/b]
[list]
[*]Player is moving (position changed between ticks)
[*]Player has been idle for less than the threshold duration
[/list]

[b]Special Behavior - Cutscene Pause (When Enabled):[/b]
When "Pause Timer During Cutscenes" is enabled, the idle timer pauses (but doesn't reset) during:
[list]
[*]Game events and cutscenes (Game1.eventUp or Game1.CurrentEvent)
[*]NPC dialogue interactions (DialogueBox active)
[*]Active NPC speakers (Game1.currentSpeaker)
[/list]

This prevents the timer from counting time during scripted sequences where the player cannot move, preserving accumulated idle time and preventing automation from starting mid-cutscene.

[line]

[size=5][b]Performance Impact[/b][/size]

[b]Before (Vanilla Automate):[/b]
[list]
[*]100+ machine groups: ~5-15% CPU usage constantly
[*]Lag spikes when entering new areas
[*]FPS drops during intensive automation
[*]Background processing even in mines, town, etc.
[/list]

[b]After (With Idle Detection Enabled):[/b]
[list]
[*]While moving: 0% CPU from Automate (completely disabled)
[*]While idle (8+ seconds): Normal Automate functionality resumes
[*]During cutscenes: Automation paused (if configured)
[*]No background processing during active gameplay
[/list]

[b]Best suited for:[/b]
[list]
[*]Large automation setups (50+ machines)
[*]Players using multiple farm expansion mods
[*]Players experiencing lag from Automate
[*]Lower-end hardware
[*]Multiplayer hosts with multiple automated farms
[/list]

[line]

[size=5][b]Example Scenarios[/b][/size]

[size=4][b]Scenario 1: Active Farming[/b][/size]
You're running around your farm planting crops, watering, and harvesting.
[list]
[*]Automate is [b]completely disabled[/b] during all movement
[*]Zero CPU overhead from machine processing
[*]You stop at a chest to organize items
[*]After 8 seconds of standing still, automation kicks in
[*]All machines process their queues while you sort inventory
[*]You start moving again - automation immediately stops
[/list]

[size=4][b]Scenario 2: Exploring Mines[/b][/size]
You're in the Skull Cavern fighting monsters.
[list]
[*]Automate is [b]not running at all[/b]
[*]Your machines back at the farm are not being scanned
[*]No CPU cycles wasted on automation processing
[*]You return to farm and stand still for 8 seconds
[*]Automation resumes and processes everything that accumulated
[/list]

[size=4][b]Scenario 3: Cutscene Protection[/b][/size]
You're watching a heart event with an NPC.
[list]
[*]You had been idle for 5 seconds (timer at 300 ticks)
[*]Cutscene starts - timer [b]pauses[/b] at 300 ticks
[*]Cutscene runs for 60 seconds
[*]Cutscene ends - timer [b]resumes[/b] from 300 ticks
[*]After 3 more seconds (480 total ticks = 8 seconds), automation starts
[*]You didn't lose your accumulated idle time
[/list]

[line]

[size=5][b]Statistics and Monitoring[/b][/size]

When Debug Mode is enabled, the mod logs performance statistics every 60 seconds to the SMAPI console:

[code]
=== Automate No More Lag - Statistics ===
Automate Cycles Checked: 3600
Automate Cycles Processed: 180
Automate Cycles FULLY STOPPED: 3420 (95.0%)
Player Idle Status: IDLE (Ticks since move: 520)
Performance Mode: ZERO OVERHEAD when moving!
==========================================
[/code]

This shows:
[list]
[*]Total automation cycles that occurred
[*]How many actually ran (when player was idle)
[*]How many were completely prevented (when player was moving)
[*]Current player idle status
[*]Ticks since last movement
[/list]

[line]

[size=5][b]Frequently Asked Questions[/b][/size]

[size=4][b]Q: Will my machines still work?[/b][/size]
A: Yes. Machines continue to process normally when you're idle (standing still for 8+ seconds). The mod only stops automation during active movement - your machines don't lose items or break.

[size=4][b]Q: What if I want automation while moving?[/b][/size]
A: Disable "Only Process When Idle" in the config. The mod will do nothing and Automate will function normally.

[size=4][b]Q: Does this work with modded machines?[/b][/size]
A: Yes. The mod patches Automate itself, not individual machines. Any machine compatible with Automate works with this mod.

[size=4][b]Q: Will items get stuck in machines?[/b][/size]
A: No. When automation resumes (after you stand still for 8 seconds), Automate processes everything normally. Items are never lost or stuck.

[size=4][b]Q: How much performance improvement will I see?[/b][/size]
A: Depends on your setup size. Small setups (10-20 machines) may see minimal improvement. Large setups (100+ machines) can see 50-95% reduction in Automate CPU usage during active gameplay.

[size=4][b]Q: Does this affect multiplayer?[/b][/size]
A: Each player needs the mod installed. The mod only affects Automate processing on your local game instance. In multiplayer, if you're the host with massive automation, this mod will reduce server lag significantly.

[size=4][b]Q: Can I adjust the idle delay?[/b][/size]
A: Yes, from 0-10 seconds via Generic Mod Config Menu. 0 seconds = automation starts instantly when you stop moving. 10 seconds = maximum delay before automation resumes.

[size=4][b]Q: What if I don't want the timer to pause during cutscenes?[/b][/size]
A: Disable "Pause Timer During Cutscenes" in the config. The timer will continue counting even during events and dialogue.

[line]

[list]
[*]Compatible with all versions of Automate

[*]Compatible with all farm expansion mods
[*]Safe to add to existing saves
[*]Safe to remove from saves
[*]No save file modifications

[/list]

[line]

[size=5][b]Technical Details[/b][/size]

[b]Harmony Patch Points:[/b]
[list]
[*]Primary: [font=Courier New]Pathoschild.Stardew.Automate.Framework.MachineManager[/font] automation methods
[*]Fallback: [font=Courier New]Pathoschild.Stardew.Automate.Framework.MachineGroup.Automate()[/font]
[/list]

[b]Update Tick Handler:[/b]
Runs every game tick to update idle detection state. Minimal overhead (simple position comparison and integer increment).

[b]Cutscene Detection:[/b]
Checks [font=Courier New]Game1.eventUp[/font], [font=Courier New]Game1.CurrentEvent[/font], [font=Courier New]Game1.activeClickableMenu[/font] type, and [font=Courier New]Game1.currentSpeaker[/font] to determine if player is in a cutscene/dialogue.
[center][/center]
